title: Attention Is All You Need
hook: The paper behind today's chatbots lists its eight authors in random order.
peek: In 2017 eight Google researchers published a short paper on machine translation. It introduced the Transformer, the design inside most modern chatbots, and it came with a footnote saying the order of their names was random.
lede: In 2017 a team of eight researchers, mostly at Google, published a paper called "Attention Is All You Need". It described the Transformer, a new way for computers to handle language, and it became one of the most cited papers of the century. Its first footnote says something rare: every author contributed equally, and the order of their names is random.

bullets.text: The footnote goes on to say who did what, from writing the first code to proposing the core idea. Listing names at random was a way of saying the work was truly shared, which is unusual in a field where first place on a paper matters a great deal.

The title riffs on the Beatles song "All You Need Is Love". Co-author Llion Jones is credited with suggesting it, because the paper's claim was that one mechanism, called attention, could do the job on its own.

Older systems read a sentence one word at a time. The Transformer lets every word look at every other word at once and decide which ones matter for its meaning, which also made training much faster on modern chips.

The paper set out to improve machine translation, testing English to German and English to French. The design spread to almost everything, and the T in GPT stands for Transformer. All eight authors left Google at some point, several to start their own companies.
